findings: An infiltrative pancreatic cancer measuring 60 mm is observed in the body of the pancreas. Serosal invasion and retropancreatic tissue invasion are noted. There is contact of more than 180° with the superior mesenteric vein, suggesting invasion. The tumor extends beyond the inferior border of the duodenum, with invasion into the colon observed. No other local invasion factors are identified. Lymph node metastases are observed in two nodes each at stations 9 and 10. A contrast-enhancing mass with surrounding edema is noted in the left centrum semiovale, raising suspicion of brain metastasis.

responses.content:
Task 1: Diagnose the local invasion factors of pancreatic cancer.

CH0 (no invasion of the common hepatic artery)
DU1 (invasion of the duodenum)
S1 (serosal invasion)
RP1 (retropancreatic tissue invasion)
PV0 (no invasion of the portal vein)
A0 (no invasion of the abdominal aorta)
PL0 (no invasion of the pancreatic lymphatic vessels)
OO1 (invasion of the colon)

Task 2: Determine the classification for local invasion (T classification) of pancreatic cancer.

Based on the size of the tumor (60 mm) and the extent of local invasion, the T classification is T4.

Task 3: Determine the N classification of pancreatic cancer.

Regional lymph nodes for pancreatic cancer in the body of the pancreas are:
- Station 9 (left gastric artery)
- Station 10 (common hepatic artery)
- Station 11 (proper hepatic artery)
- Station 12 (gastroduodenal artery)
- Station 13 (right gastric artery)
- Station 14 (common bile duct)
- Station 15 (cystic duct)
- Station 16 (hilar lymph nodes)
- Station 17 (pericholedochal lymph nodes)
- Station 18 (peripancreatic lymph nodes)

The patient's metastatic lymph node stations are:
- Station 9
- Station 10

Both stations are regional for the tumor location in the body of the pancreas. Counting only the metastatic lymph nodes within the regional stations, there are 4 metastatic lymph nodes (2 in station 9 and 2 in station 10). Therefore, the N classification is N1b.

Task 4: Determine the M classification of pancreatic cancer.

The presence of a contrast-enhancing mass with surrounding edema in the left centrum semiovale, raising suspicion of brain metastasis, indicates distant metastasis. Therefore, the M classification is M1.

Task 5: Determine the resectability classification of pancreatic cancer.

Based on the results of Task 1 and Task 4, the tumor is unresectable due to distant metastasis. Therefore, the resectability classification is Unresectable (UR).

Task 6: Determine the overall stage according to the JPS staging system.

Based on the determined T (T4), N (N1b), and M (M1) categories, the overall stage is Stage IV.
